question: Slovo alkohol pochádza z arabčiny, no pôvodne neoznačovalo nápoj, ale jemný čierny prášok. Na čo ho ľudia používali?
source_excerpt: Arabic al-kuḥl, a fine powder of antimony used as eyeliner; sense later extended to essence and spirit of wine.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone assumes 'alcohol' always meant a drink. It actually began as eye make-up. The stem's footholds ('fine black powder', use by people) let the player reason toward cosmetics, which gives a proud near-miss or an 'aha'.
extra.verification_notes: Alcohol derives from Arabic al-kuḥl, a fine dark antimony powder used as eyeliner/eye cosmetic (https://en.wiktionary.com/wiki/alcohol).

explanation: Arabské al-kuhl bol prášok na zvýraznenie očí, dnes ho poznáme ako kajal. Alchymisti tak neskôr začali volať každú jemne vyčistenú „podstatu“, až napokon aj čistý lieh z vína.

question: Tulipány sa do Európy dostali z Osmanskej ríše a spolu s nimi aj ich názov. Pochádza z tureckého slova pre vec, ktorú ľudia nosili na hlave a ktorej sa kvet tvarom podobá. Čo to bolo?
source_excerpt: from Ottoman Turkish دلبند (tülbent, dülbent, cheesecloth), from Classical Persian دلبند (dulband, turban)

extra.why_interesting: Players treat 'tulipán' as a plain flower name, often tied to Holland. Its root is actually a word for headwear, and with the Ottoman and 'worn on the head' footholds they can work out which one.
extra.verification_notes: Standard etymology: tulip derives via Ottoman Turkish tülbent from Persian dulband 'turban', and the flower's shape resembles a turban (https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/tulip).

explanation: Zatvorený kvet tulipánu Európanom pripomínal zamotaný turban. Samotní Turci však tulipán volajú úplne inak, a to lale.
